title: Optimization request qualification checklist and timebox play
creator: Priya Menon
description: Create a repeatable qualification checklist and a timeboxed 'play' for incoming optimization/advisory requests (non-bug). Focus on batching/caching knobs, quantization profile recommendations, and routing policy guidance for enterprise customers. Deliverables: intake form fields, automated pre-score, routing rules to advisory lanes (self-serve, concierge, escalation), expected SLA/timeboxes for each lane, sample config templates, and handoff artifacts for Eng/DevEx.
acceptance_criteria: A public intake form (Confluence + support portal) with required fields to triage optimization requests: workload profile, traffic percentile, cost target, current model & quantization, target latency, legal constraints.
Automated pre-score algorithm defined (inputs + weightings) and a mock script to demonstrate sample scores on 10 customer examples.
Routing rules documented: Self-serve (docs + config suggestions), Concierge (1–2 week timebox), Escalation (SLA-backed engagement) with SLAs for response/first-assessment.

Three sample configuration templates for common asks: (1) latency-first batching/caching, (2) cost-first quantization profile recommendation, (3) geo-aware routing fallback policy. Each template includes expected token-cost delta and risk notes.
Handoff checklist created for Eng/DevEx with required artifacts and a GitHub issue template to kick off work in Dedicated/Private environments.
Stakeholder sign-off from Support, Solutions Eng, and Runtime team on playbook and timeboxes.
plan: Week 1: Kickoff with Support, Solutions Eng, Runtime and Security to align scope and constraints.
Week 1: Draft intake form fields and sample customer artifact checklist.
Week 2: Define scoring rubric and weightings; run mock scoring on saved anonymized requests.
Week 2: Draft routing lanes and SLA matrix; create initial timebox templates (3 day, 10 day, 30 day).
Week 3: Produce three sample config templates and engineering handoff checklist.
Week 3: Review with stakeholders; iterate on feedback and finalize Confluence page + support portal integration.
Week 4: Pilot with 5 active customers; measure accuracy of pre-score and timebox adherence; iterate.
Post-pilot: Prepare rollout plan and partner with Growth to expose the self-serve lane in docs.
required_customer_artifacts: Representative traffic profile (qps, average & P95 token length)
Current model name + version and any applied quantization details
Sample prompts (5–10) and expected outputs or quality metrics
Privacy/regulatory constraints or data residency requirements
Access details for logs/metrics or a dashboard snapshot (if available)
routing_rules_summary: Requests are automatically pre-scored (0–100). Score < 30 -> self-serve (docs + suggestion engine); 30–70 -> Concierge (timeboxed up to 10 business days, Solutions Eng + limited runtime experiments); >70 or high customer_impact -> Escalation (SLA-backed engagement, dedicated cross-functional pod). Critical enterprise with contract SLAs bypasses auto-lane and goes straight to Escalation.
scoring_rubric: Business impact (0–30): revenue at risk, number of affected seats, compliance risk.
Technical complexity (0–30): need for custom quantization, model refactor, infra changes.
Observability availability (0–20): presence of traces/metrics/sample logs to reproduce issue.
Time sensitivity (0–10): requested by deadline, product launch, or regulatory need.
Customer maturity/contract tier (0–10): enterprise/priority customers weighted higher.
